original.target_description: Experiment 3 racial-identity outcome in a 2 (participant race: African American or White) × 2 (fairness cue: high or low) design; specific target test unresolved.

notes: Identity verified from title page: Social Identity Contingencies: How Diversity Cues Signal Threat or Safety for African Americans in Mainstream Institutions; Valerie Purdie-Vaughns, Claude M. Steele, Paul G. Davies, Ruth Ditlmann, Jennifer Randall Crosby; Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 2008, 94(4), 615–630; DOI 10.1037/0022-3514.94.4.615. Supplied canonical text is a full primary research article with methods, results, references and appendices, rather than an abstract or secondary account. No PDF path was supplied; no rendering or acquisition performed. Canonical extraction has symbol substitutions (e.g. equals rendered as double quote, inequality as #); quotations preserve these literally. The neutral description identifies Experiment 3 racial identity and fairness but does not specify the omnibus fairness effect, race effect, interaction, African American simple effect, or White simple effect. Racial Identity results are printed on journal p. 626; journal p. 625 (eleventh article page) gives the measure and other distinct outcomes. No target chosen from numerical agreement or input order. Candidates on p. 626: race main effect F(1, 73) = 51.03, p = .001; fairness main effect F(1, 73) = 6.49, p = .01; Race × Fairness interaction F < 1, no numeric p printed; African American high/low fairness comparison F(1, 73) = 5.09, p = .03, printed eta-squared glyph %2 = .07; White high/low fairness comparison F < 2, printed %2 = .03, no numeric p printed. Equality and upper-bound readings follow canonical symbol context; no effect conversion performed. Requested test-statistic metric cannot select between these tests. Candidate full-model sample: p. 624 explicitly reports final analysis of 77 participants (40 African American, 37 White), after dropping 12 identifying as other ethnic groups and 1 not following directions from 90 recruited. The 77 is explicitly printed, not inferred from degrees of freedom and not a derived sum. These are participant counts, not observations or clusters. Retained only as candidate evidence in the n disposition because requested row/test correspondence remains unresolved. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
